ev.ane_m_flood.text: The Nile turned reddish-brown and began to rise: the flood has come. The fields vanished under water, the village became an island, and now you visit the neighbours by boat.
ev.ane_m_opet.text: The Opet festival: priests carry the barque of Amun from Karnak to Luxor, and bread and beer are handed out along the way. You stood half the day in the crowd for a glimpse of the god's closed shrine.
ev.ane_m_valley_feast.text: The Beautiful Festival of the Valley: families cross to the west bank and feast right beside the tombs of their ancestors. People sang, ate, left flowers for the dead – and nobody spoke of sad things.
ev.ane_m_child_beer.text: For the first time you got beer in your own cup, like the grown-ups. It is thick, sweetish and full of bread crumbs – here everyone drinks it, from toddlers to old men.
ev.ane_m_sidelock.text: They shaved your head again, leaving just one braid at the side – the "sidelock of youth". All children wear it: it's cooler, and there are fewer lice.
ev.ane_m_cat.text: In the night the cat killed a snake in the storeroom and proudly left it at the door in the morning. Cats are loved and protected here: they belong to Bastet and guard the grain.
ev.ane_m_kohl.text: Every morning you line your eyes with black kohl, as men and women both do. They say it protects against the sun and flies – and it looks good too.
ev.ane_m_senet.text: You spent the whole evening moving pieces on a senet board with a neighbour. You lost three times, but he swears the game pleases the gods and will come in handy in the afterlife.
ev.ane_m_apis.text: The living Apis bull was led through the streets of Memphis – black, with a white mark on his forehead. People reached out to touch the ground where he had walked.
ev.ane_m_harbor_ships.text: In the harbour of Peru-nefer they are unloading ships from Byblos: cedar logs, jars of oil, bearded sailors speaking a foreign tongue. You stood on the quay until evening.
ev.ane_m_pyramids.text: Someone took you to the desert's edge to see the pyramids. They are over a thousand years old, their casing is crumbling, and the Sphinx is buried in sand up to its chest. Even the old folk can't say who built them.
ev.ane_m_hippo.text: A hippo climbed out of the river at night and trampled half the lentil field. In the morning the neighbours banged copper pots, but he only yawned and slid back into the water.
ev.ane_m_sand_bread.text: Grit crunched in your bread again. Flour from the millstones is full of stone dust, and old people's teeth are worn nearly to the gums. You'd better learn to chew carefully too.
ev.ane_m_khamsin.text: For three days a hot wind blew from the desert. Sand got into your eyes, the jars, the bed. Everyone stayed home with rags stuffed under the doors.
ev.ane_m_love_song.text: Someone by the river was singing a love song: "My sister, the only one, there is none like her…" – that is what lovers call each other here. You hummed it to yourself all evening.
ev.ane_m_wine_label.text: At a banquet the wine came in a jar labelled: "Year 5. Good wine of the estate of Amun, western river. Vintner Nenna." The guests argued over whether it had been a good year.
ev.ane_m_mourners.text: A funeral procession went by: oxen dragged the coffin on a sledge, followed by mourning women with loosened hair, throwing dust on their heads. A rich man was going to the west bank.
ev.ane_m_ostracon.text: A neighbour sent you a note on a potsherd, asking for the basket you borrowed before the flood and reminding you that you owe him two jars of beer. On the west bank there are more potsherds than papyrus.
ev.ane_m_akitu.text: New Year: the statue of Marduk is carried out of Esagila and along the Processional Way. The city celebrates for twelve days, then picks up its hoes again.
ev.ane_m_dates.text: Date harvest: young men with a rope around their waists climb the palms while others catch the heavy bunches below. In the evening they boiled date syrup, and the whole yard smelled sweet.
ev.ane_m_straw_beer.text: The neighbours drank beer from a shared jar through long reed straws, to keep the husks out. They gave you a straw too – and another story about somebody's mother-in-law.
ev.ane_m_envelope.text: A letter arrived: a clay tablet inside a clay envelope stamped with a seal. To read it, you have to break the envelope. You cracked it carefully, the way you were taught.
ev.ane_m_seal.text: A seal-cutter made you a stone cylinder seal of your own: a god, a worshipper and your name. Now you can seal contracts like a grown and respected person.
ev.ane_m_kudurru.text: A boundary stone, a kudurru, was set up at the edge of a field: symbols of the gods at the top, curses at the bottom on anyone who moves the boundary. Even people who can't read give it a wide berth.
ev.ane_m_kassite_horses.text: Kassite grooms were running a herd of young horses across the meadow. The Kassites know horses better than anyone, and even the kings of distant Egypt ask them for chariot teams as gifts.
ev.ane_m_assur_cliff.text: From the wall on the cliff you can see the Tigris bend around the rock and the steppe stretch to the horizon beyond. They say the god Ashur and the city are one and the same.
ev.ane_m_spring_flood.text: In spring the river swelled with mountain snow and broke a dyke upstream. All night the men hauled baskets of earth. Here the water doesn't feed you by itself – you fight it.
ev.ane_m_gilgamesh.text: An old man by the hearth told the tale of Gilgamesh: how he sought immortality, found the plant of eternal youth and lost it to a snake while bathing. "So live now," he finished.
ev.ane_m_onions.text: Lunch in the field: a flatbread, an onion, a handful of garlic and a jug of beer for everyone. The onion crunches, your eyes water, and it's the best meal in the world.
ev.ane_m_reed_boat.text: You and the other kids tied a little boat out of reeds and paddled along the canal until it tipped over. You dried off in the sun eating stolen cucumbers.
ev.ane_m_school_stick.text: The teacher hit you with his stick again for a blot. "A boy's ear is on his back – he listens when he is beaten," the teachers like to say. You do remember the signs better, though.
ev.ane_m_bes_amulet.text: You hung an amulet of the dwarf god Bes and the hippo goddess Taweret over the bed. They protect women in childbirth and newborns, and it feels safer with them there.
ev.ane_m_nubian_gold.text: Barges arrived from the south with tribute from Kush: gold in rings, ivory, leopard skins and a live giraffe. Scribes on the quay counted everything down to the last ring.
ev.ane_m_captive_song.text: In the evening the captives from the north sang a song about mountains and home in their own tongue. The overseer didn't understand the words and let them be. You sang along without knowing where you came from yourself.
ev.ane_d_corvee.substitute: Pay someone to go in your place
ev.ane_d_corvee.hide: Hide in the marshes until autumn
ev.ane_d_corvee.hide.success: The scribe moved on, and nobody searched the marshes.
ev.ane_d_corvee.hide.failure: They found you. You had to work double, and your family paid a fine.
ev.ane_d_corvee.title: Labour duty
ev.ane_d_corvee.text: A scribe with a muster list is going round the village: every man must give a season to the king's works, hauling stone and digging canals. At home, sowing is just beginning.
ev.ane_d_scribe_school.title: Scribal school
ev.ane_d_scribe_school.text: An old scribe is taking pupils: years of copying instructions on potsherds, enduring the stick and memorising hundreds of signs. But a scribe, they say, is "his own master" and never hauls stone.
ev.ane_d_scribe_school.text.babylon: The temple runs a "tablet house": years of copying sign lists and old Sumerian hymns, enduring the stick and memorising hundreds of cuneiform signs. But a scribe is a respected man.
ev.ane_d_scribe_school.text.assur: The temple runs a "tablet house": years of copying sign lists and old hymns, enduring the stick and memorising hundreds of cuneiform signs. But a scribe is a respected man.
ev.ane_d_scribe_school_later.title: A scribe's post
ev.ane_d_scribe_school_later.text: Your old teacher has not forgotten you: the granary needs a scribe who can count sacks and not muddle his signs. A post like this is for life.
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.gift: Treat the scribe to beer and a goose
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.gift.success: After the goose, the field shrank miraculously.
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.gift.failure: The scribe ate the goose and still wrote down the full tax – plus a bit extra "for trying".
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.protest.success: They measured again, and the field was indeed smaller. The neighbours look at you with respect.
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.protest.failure: You were beaten with sticks for your insolence, and the tax stayed the same.
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.title: The scribe with the rope
ev.ane_d_harvest_tax.text: The scribes have come with their measuring rope to survey your field and decide how much grain you owe the temple. Their chief looks at your field as if it were twice its size.
ev.ane_d_oracle.ask.success: The statue "nodded" at the neighbour. The cauldron turned up under his straw.
ev.ane_d_oracle.ask.failure: The statue drew back. The neighbour is triumphant, and you are left without the cauldron and looking a fool.
ev.ane_d_oracle.title: Judgement of the god
ev.ane_d_oracle.text: A good copper cauldron of yours has vanished, and you suspect a neighbour. Tomorrow the statue of the deified king Amenhotep will be carried through the village: you can put a question to it, and the bearers will lurch forward for "yes" or back for "no".
ev.ane_d_oracle_grudge.reconcile: Invite him for beer and make peace
ev.ane_d_oracle_grudge.kenbet: Take him to the elders' court for slander
ev.ane_d_oracle_grudge.kenbet.success: The court made him swear by the king's name never to slander you again.
ev.ane_d_oracle_grudge.kenbet.failure: No witnesses came forward, and the court only laughed at your quarrel.
ev.ane_d_oracle_grudge.title: An old grudge
ev.ane_d_oracle_grudge.text: The neighbour whom the god once accused in front of everyone has never forgiven you. Now he tells the village you bribed the statue's bearers.
ev.ane_d_donkey.court.success: The court awarded you a better donkey and half a sack of grain besides.
ev.ane_d_donkey.court.failure: The neighbour brought three witnesses who "saw" the donkey limping before.
ev.ane_d_donkey.heal: Nurse the donkey and drop it
ev.ane_d_donkey.title: The lame donkey
ev.ane_d_donkey.text: You hired your donkey out to a neighbour for a month, and he brought it back lame and refuses to pay: "It was lame already." The local court, the kenbet of respected neighbours, sits on the fifth day.
ev.ane_d_ordeal.plunge.success: The river brought you back to the bank. Now the neighbour must answer for her false charge.
ev.ane_d_ordeal.plunge.failure: They pulled you out barely alive. The judges took it as a sign of guilt and imposed a fine.
ev.ane_d_ordeal.title: Ordeal by the river
ev.ane_d_ordeal.text: A neighbour has accused you of witchcraft: her goats have stopped giving milk. There are no witnesses, and the judges have decided to leave it to the river: if the river takes you, you are guilty; if it brings you out, you are clean.
ev.ane_d_pledge.temple: Borrow from the temple at interest
ev.ane_d_pledge.flee.success: You left by night, and in a strange city nobody asks about debts.
ev.ane_d_pledge.flee.failure: You were caught at the ferry and brought back to the creditor in disgrace.
ev.ane_d_pledge.title: The pledge
ev.ane_d_pledge.text: The creditor demands the barley you borrowed in a hungry year. By custom a debtor may give himself or a member of his household as a pledge, to work in the creditor's house until the debt is paid.
ev.ane_d_pledge_free.stay: Stay on with him as a paid worker
ev.ane_d_pledge_free.title: The debt is worked off
ev.ane_d_pledge_free.text: The years in a stranger's house are over: the creditor's scribe has broken the tablet recording your debt. You are your own master again.
ev.ane_d_temple_barley.title: Barley on loan
ev.ane_d_temple_barley.text: The harvest is far off and the bins are empty. The temple lends barley: repay it after the harvest with a third on top. The scribe already has a tablet ready.
ev.ane_d_temple_barley_due.delay.success: The scribe agreed to wait for the rest until next harvest.
ev.ane_d_temple_barley_due.delay.failure: You got your extension, but the debt grew, and now you are in debt.
ev.ane_d_temple_barley_due.title: Repayment due
ev.ane_d_temple_barley_due.text: The harvest is in, and the temple scribe is at the gate with your tablet: the barley plus a third.
ev.ane_d_extispicy.title: Ask the gods
ev.ane_d_extispicy.text: You are planning something big: a long journey and a large deal. A baru diviner offers to sacrifice a lamb and read the answer of Shamash and Adad in its liver. It doesn't come cheap.
ev.ane_d_caravan.title: A long voyage
ev.ane_d_caravan.text: A temple trading agent is fitting out a ship for Byblos: linen and grain out, cedar, oil and wine back. You can put in your own goods for a share.
ev.ane_d_caravan.text.babylon: Merchants are gathering a caravan down the river to the Gulf, to Dilmun: barley and wool out, copper and pearls back. You can put in your own goods for a share.
ev.ane_d_caravan.text.assur: Merchants are gathering a caravan west, to the Euphrates and on to Carchemish: textiles and tin out, silver back. You can put in your own goods for a share.
ev.ane_d_caravan_back.see.success: Everything arrived and sold: your share came back more than doubled.
ev.ane_d_caravan_back.see.failure: The cargo was lost – some say a storm, some say bandits. Your share went with it.
ev.ane_d_caravan_back.pray.success: The gods were kind: the profit nearly doubled your stake.
ev.ane_d_caravan_back.pray.failure: Prayers didn't help: the cargo was lost on the way.
ev.ane_d_caravan_back.title: News of the venture
ev.ane_d_caravan_back.text: News has come of your share in the long venture. You go to find out how it ended.
ev.ane_d_tomb_prep.cheap: Buy a ready-made scroll and add your name
ev.ane_d_tomb_prep.maat: Better to live by maat, truth
ev.ane_d_tomb_prep.title: House of eternity
ev.ane_d_tomb_prep.text: It is time to think of eternity. Craftsmen offer a painted coffin with your name on it and a scroll of the "Book of Coming Forth by Day" – spells so that your heart will not testify against you at the judgement of Osiris.
ev.ane_d_tomb_robbed.hunt: Hunt the thieves through the mayor
ev.ane_d_tomb_robbed.hunt.success: The thieves were caught and some of the goods returned.
ev.ane_d_tomb_robbed.hunt.failure: The mayor shrugged: "Hundreds of tombs like yours are being robbed these days."
ev.ane_d_tomb_robbed.title: Thieves in the tomb
ev.ane_d_tomb_robbed.text: The necropolis guard came running: thieves broke into the family tomb, stripped the gilding from the coffin and carried off the bronze vessels.
ev.ane_d_beer_house.title: The beer house
ev.ane_d_beer_house.text: Your teacher says, "You wander from street to street where it smells of beer, and beer destroys your soul." But your friends are calling you to the beer house, where they play the lute and nobody asks about lessons.
ev.ane_d_runaway.run.success: You slipped past the fortress at night. You are free, though far from everything you know.
ev.ane_d_runaway.run.failure: You were caught at the fortress and returned to your master. The punishment was harsh.
ev.ane_d_runaway.title: Escape
ev.ane_d_runaway.text: Two captives from your household plan to run north, past the border fortress, back to their hills. They ask you to come. The frontier scribes write down everyone who passes.
ev.ane_d_adoption.leave: Take your freedom but go your own way
ev.ane_d_adoption.title: Adoption
ev.ane_d_adoption.text: Your mistress, a childless widow, has declared before witnesses that she adopts the children of her slave woman and frees them, and gives the eldest in marriage to her younger kinsman. You are among them.
ev.ane_d_recruit.hide.success: The levy went by without you.
ev.ane_d_recruit.hide.failure: They found you and enrolled you – first into the line and last to the cooking pot.
ev.ane_d_recruit.title: The levy
ev.ane_d_recruit.text: The scribe of recruits is back in the village: the king needs archers for a campaign. They take the young, at least one from each family. Someone has already pointed at you.
ev.ane_d_horses.title: A chariot team
ev.ane_d_horses.text: A dealer has brought a pair of fine horses from the north. With a team like that you could serve in the chariotry – or simply drive through town so everyone turns to look.
ev.ane_d_shaduf.build: Chip in and grow onions and cucumbers
ev.ane_d_shaduf.title: A shaduf by the canal
ev.ane_d_shaduf.text: The neighbours suggest chipping in for a shaduf by the canal – a pole with a bucket and a clay counterweight. With it you can water a vegetable plot even in the dry months.
ev.ane_d_shaduf_harvest.title: The garden pays
ev.ane_d_shaduf_harvest.text: The shaduf by the canal creaks every day, and your plot has become the best in the village. Onions, cucumbers and lettuce sell at market faster than you can lay them out.
ev.ane_d_inheritance_court.court: Go to court with the records
ev.ane_d_inheritance_court.court.success: The scribes found the record of the land division from your grandfather's day. The field is yours.
ev.ane_d_inheritance_court.court.failure: The records were "lost", and the relative turned out to have friends among the scribes.
ev.ane_d_inheritance_court.title: Inherited land
ev.ane_d_inheritance_court.text: A distant relative claims that the field you inherited is really his. In Egypt a woman can own land and go to court herself – and you can demand the old records from the treasury.
ev.ane_d_veil.report: Take her to the palace gate
ev.ane_d_veil.look_away.success: Nobody noticed anything. You hope she makes it home.
ev.ane_d_veil.look_away.failure: A neighbour saw you walk past and reported it. You were beaten and fined.
ev.ane_d_veil.title: The veil
ev.ane_d_veil.text: In the street you notice a slave woman wearing a veil. By the law of Assur only free married women may go veiled in the street – and whoever sees and keeps quiet is punished too.
ev.ane_d_will.reward: Give more to those who cared for you
ev.ane_d_will.temple: Leave part to the temple for offerings
ev.ane_d_will.title: The will
ev.ane_d_will.text: You are old, and it is time to declare before witnesses who gets what. Not all the children cared for you equally in your old age. The law lets you pass over the ungrateful.
ev.ane_d_low_nile.hope.success: It turned out all right: the temple granaries opened for handouts.
ev.ane_d_low_nile.hope.failure: The spring was a hungry one.
ev.ane_d_low_nile.canal: Save water: clear the canals with the neighbours
ev.ane_d_low_nile.title: A weak flood
ev.ane_d_low_nile.text: The Nile barely rose this year. The higher fields stayed dry, and the price of barley climbs every week. The old folk remember the hungry years.
ev.ane_d_wet_nurse.title: Wet nurse
ev.ane_d_wet_nurse.text: The steward of a great house is looking for a wet nurse for a newborn heir. In Egypt a wet nurse is almost family: her children are later called the "milk brothers" of the masters, and that opens many doors.
ev.ane_t_tomb_robbers.report.success: The thieves were caught red-handed. The mayor of Thebes remembers your name.
ev.ane_t_tomb_robbers.report.failure: The mayor waved you away: the thieves had protectors. And they found out who talked.
ev.ane_t_tomb_robbers.title: A night-time offer
ev.ane_t_tomb_robbers.text: A stonecutter you've known since childhood whispers that they've found a way into an old royal tomb. There's enough gold in there for a lifetime. They need one more man with a strong back – and a tight mouth.
ev.ane_t_robbery_trial.deny.success: You endured the beating and said nothing. They let you go for lack of evidence.
ev.ane_t_robbery_trial.deny.failure: You were found guilty. Everything was taken, and you were sent to the quarries.
ev.ane_t_robbery_trial.title: The interrogation
ev.ane_t_robbery_trial.text: One of your accomplices was caught and, beaten under questioning, named names. The vizier has convened a court. Now it is your turn.
ev.ane_t_captured.ransom.success: A year later you were ransomed in an exchange of prisoners.
ev.ane_t_captured.ransom.failure: No ransom came. You were sold into a foreign household.
ev.ane_t_captured.escape.success: You chewed through the rope and spent a week making your way back to your own side.
ev.ane_t_captured.escape.failure: You were caught. Now you are a slave in a foreign land.
ev.ane_t_captured.title: Captured
ev.ane_t_captured.text: In battle your unit was surrounded, and you found yourself among the prisoners. The enemy ties your arms behind your back and drives you toward their land.
ev.ane_t_gold_valor.title: Gold of valour
ev.ane_t_gold_valor.text: After the campaign the king rewards those who distinguished themselves. The herald calls your name: for bravery you receive the "gold of valour" – and you may ask for one more favour.
ev.ane_t_accused_eg.defend.success: You caught the lie in his testimony, and the judges turned the punishment on him.
ev.ane_t_accused_eg.defend.failure: The judges believed him. A fine, a beating and disgrace.
ev.ane_t_accused_eg.title: A false accusation
ev.ane_t_accused_eg.text: A man you quarrelled with has informed that you stole grain from a royal granary. You are summoned before the judges. He has found witnesses; you have only the truth.
ev.ane_t_accused_mes.defend.success: You caught the lie in his testimony, and the judges turned the punishment on him.
ev.ane_t_accused_mes.defend.failure: The judges believed him. A fine, a beating and disgrace.
ev.ane_t_accused_mes.title: A false accusation
ev.ane_t_accused_mes.text: A man you quarrelled with has informed that you stole grain from a royal granary. You are summoned before the judges. He has found witnesses; you have only the truth.
ev.ane_t_handwriting.title: A fine hand
ev.ane_t_handwriting.text: Your report reached a high official. He liked your writing and is calling you to the capital, to his chancery. Life there is different – and so are the dangers.
ev.ane_t_great_flood_eg.title: The great flood
ev.ane_t_great_flood_eg.text: The river rose above every mark. The mud-brick house soaked through and slumped, and the grain in the storeroom is ruined. The neighbours have scattered.
ev.ane_t_great_flood_eg.text.thebes: The Nile rose so high that the water reached the temples. The mud-brick house soaked through and slumped, and the grain in the storeroom is ruined. The neighbours have scattered.
ev.ane_t_great_flood_mes.title: The great flood
ev.ane_t_great_flood_mes.text: The river rose above every mark. The mud-brick house soaked through and slumped, and the grain in the storeroom is ruined. The neighbours have scattered.
ev.ane_t_great_flood_mes.text.thebes: The Nile rose so high that the water reached the temples. The mud-brick house soaked through and slumped, and the grain in the storeroom is ruined. The neighbours have scattered.
ev.ane_t_far_field_eg.title: An inheritance far away
ev.ane_t_far_field_eg.text: A letter has come: a distant relative has died childless and left you a field and a house in another region. To claim them you must move there – otherwise the temple takes them.
ev.ane_t_far_field_mes.title: An inheritance far away
ev.ane_t_far_field_mes.text: A letter has come: a distant relative has died childless and left you a field and a house in another region. To claim them you must move there – otherwise the temple takes them.
ev.ane_t_harem.title: The king's household of women
ev.ane_t_harem.text: In the king's household of women at Mi-wer, near the Fayum, they weave the finest linen in the land. The steward is looking for skilled weavers and girls of good families. Whoever goes stays a long time – perhaps for ever.
ev.ane_t_harem_plot.join.success: The plot was never uncovered, and you were well paid for your silence.
ev.ane_t_harem_plot.join.failure: The plot was uncovered. You were questioned and banished from the palace in disgrace.
ev.ane_t_harem_plot.title: Whispers in the household
ev.ane_t_harem_plot.text: One of the high-ranking wives calls you to her rooms and talks a long time about how her son deserves the throne more than the heir. She needs people to carry letters beyond the walls.
ev.ane_t_embassy.go_return: Go and come back with gifts
ev.ane_t_embassy.title: An embassy to Egypt
ev.ane_t_embassy.text: The king is sending an embassy to Pharaoh: horses, lapis lazuli, letters on clay – and a request for gold, "for in Egypt gold is as plentiful as dust". The party needs a reliable man or woman. The journey will take months.
ev.ane_t_envoy_egypt.title: An embassy to Babylon
ev.ane_t_envoy_egypt.text: Pharaoh is sending an embassy to the king of Babylon: gold, ebony, painted vessels – and a reply to his letter complaining that the last gold was adulterated. The party needs someone who can read. The journey will take months.
ev.ane_w_maryannu_officer.title: Chariot commander
ev.ane_w_maryannu_officer.text: The commander of the chariot squadron fell in a skirmish. The general is looking at you: can you handle fifty teams?
ev.ane_w_maryannu_horse.buy: Buy a new one from travelling dealers
ev.ane_w_maryannu_horse.heal.success: The horse recovered just in time to march.
ev.ane_w_maryannu_horse.heal.failure: The horse didn't recover, and you were left to guard the baggage train.
ev.ane_w_maryannu_horse.title: A lame horse
ev.ane_w_maryannu_horse.text: Right before the campaign your best horse went lame. A good horse costs as much as a whole field, and without a pair a chariot is just a cart.
ev.ane_w_tomb_rations.side: Moonlight: paint coffins for private clients
ev.ane_w_tomb_rations.complain: Go with the others to the vizier
ev.ane_w_tomb_rations.complain.success: The vizier ordered grain issued from the temple stores.
ev.ane_w_tomb_rations.complain.failure: They heard you out and sent you back empty-handed.
ev.ane_w_tomb_rations.title: Late rations
ev.ane_w_tomb_rations.text: Twenty days have passed and the gang's grain still hasn't come. The scribe of the tomb shrugs: the granaries on the west bank are empty.
ev.ane_w_tomb_chief.title: Chief of the gang
ev.ane_w_tomb_chief.text: The chief of the right side of the gang has died. The scribe of the tomb puts your name forward: you would answer for the men, the tools and every crack in the rock.
ev.ane_w_embalmer.proper: Do it properly, at your own cost
ev.ane_w_embalmer.title: A poor family
ev.ane_w_embalmer.text: A poor family brought an old man's body and everything they could scrape together. It will only pay for a quick embalming: natron and plain wrappings, no resins or amulets.
ev.ane_w_brewer_house.title: A beer house of your own
ev.ane_w_brewer_house.text: Your beer is praised up and down the street. You could rent a house by the canal, hire two helpers and brew for sale – for boatmen, scribes and anyone who wants to sit a while in the evening.
ev.ane_w_baru_omen.truth.success: The governor postponed the campaign – and thanked you later, when his neighbours walked into an ambush.
ev.ane_w_baru_omen.truth.failure: The governor flew into a rage and found another, more agreeable diviner.
ev.ane_w_baru_omen.repeat: Suggest repeating the reading with another lamb
ev.ane_w_baru_omen.flatter: Tell him what he wants to hear
ev.ane_w_baru_omen.title: An evil sign
ev.ane_w_baru_omen.text: The governor ordered you to ask the gods about a campaign. The lamb's liver is bad: the "Finger" is twisted, the "Palace Gate" closed. The governor is waiting outside – and waiting for a good answer.
ev.ane_w_baru_court.title: Diviner to the court
ev.ane_w_baru_court.text: The king needs another learned diviner to watch the moon and the omens and write reports. It is a place among the first men of the land – and under their close eye.
ev.ane_w_potter_shop.title: A kiln of your own
ev.ane_w_potter_shop.text: The temple is ordering a thousand jars for beer and wine for the festival. If you build your own kiln and take on two apprentices, the order is yours.
ev.ane_w_chantress.serve: Ask for a place in her household
ev.ane_w_chantress.modest: Bow and return to the choir
ev.ane_w_chantress.title: Before the God's Wife
ev.ane_w_chantress.text: At the festival you sing in the choir before the God's Wife of Amun, the highest priestess of Thebes. She listens closely and after the service asks your name.
ev.ane_w_boatman_obelisk.go.success: The obelisk is standing, and now you tell the story in every beer house.
ev.ane_w_boatman_obelisk.go.failure: A rope snapped and your boat capsized. You survived, but it took a long time to heal.
ev.ane_w_boatman_obelisk.title: The obelisk
ev.ane_w_boatman_obelisk.text: A granite obelisk is being shipped from Aswan to Karnak on a huge barge. They need rowers for the tow boats. The pay is triple, but if the barge breaks loose there will be nothing left to bury.
ev.ane_w_boat_owner.title: A barge of your own
ev.ane_w_boat_owner.text: An old owner is selling a sturdy acacia cargo barge. Buy it, and you can carry grain for the temple under contract and take a share instead of wages.
ev.ane_mv_to_thebes.title: Building works in Thebes
ev.ane_mv_to_thebes.text: In Thebes they are building new halls for Amun and memorial temples for the king. They are calling masons, carvers and porters: good rations and years of work.
ev.ane_mv_to_memphis.title: Downriver
ev.ane_mv_to_memphis.text: A boatman you know says that in Memphis, in the harbour where ships from Byblos and Cyprus unload, a sharp person can earn more in a year than here in five.
ev.ane_mv_to_kar_tukulti.hide.failure: They found you and drove you north with the rest.
ev.ane_mv_to_kar_tukulti.title: Craftsmen taken north
ev.ane_mv_to_kar_tukulti.text: The Assyrians who took Babylon are listing craftsmen: King Tukulti-Ninurta is building a new city across the Tigris and needs hands. Those who go willingly are promised rations and a house.
ev.ane_mv_to_babylon.title: Study in Babylon
ev.ane_mv_to_babylon.text: The best scribes and diviners train in Babylon, where the ancient tablets and omen lists are kept. A Babylonian master is willing to take you on.
ev.ane_mv_akhetaten.title: The city of the Aten
ev.ane_mv_akhetaten.text: Pharaoh Akhenaten is building a new capital on empty ground: Akhetaten, "Horizon of the Aten". The court, craftsmen and scribes are being moved there. You are offered a house and a post.
ev.ane_mv_akhetaten_end.title: The city empties
ev.ane_mv_akhetaten_end.text: Akhenaten is gone, and the court is leaving Akhetaten. Houses stand empty, workshops are abandoned with statues half-finished. It is time for you to go too.
ev.ane_f_aten.aten: Pray to the Aten as the king commands
ev.ane_f_aten.secret: Keep your Amun amulets in secret
ev.ane_f_aten.both: Argue with no one and carry on
ev.ane_f_aten.title: Only the Aten
ev.ane_f_aten.text: Pharaoh's men go from temple to temple chiselling the name of Amun from the walls. From now on only the Aten is to be honoured – the sun disc whose rays end in open hands. The old priests say nothing.
ev.ane_f_stela.title: A stela with ears
ev.ane_f_stela.text: You were ill a long time and promised Meretseger, "She who loves silence", a gift if you recovered. The craftsmen carve little stelae with ears – so the god can hear your prayer better.
ev.ane_f_akitu_king.title: The king is slapped
ev.ane_f_akitu_king.text: On the fifth day of the festival the high priest takes the king's regalia from him and strikes his cheek: if tears come, Marduk is pleased and the year will be good. You stand in the crowd by the temple.
ev.ane_f_shamash_oath.title: An oath by Shamash
ev.ane_f_shamash_oath.text: A partner claims you owe him silver. The tablet is lost. The judges propose that you both swear in the temple of Shamash, god of the sun and of justice – whoever lies will be cursed.
ev.ane_f_foreign_in_egypt.convert: Take up the gods of Egypt
ev.ane_f_foreign_in_egypt.keep: Keep the faith of your ancestors
ev.ane_f_foreign_in_egypt.title: Foreign gods
ev.ane_f_foreign_in_egypt.text: You pray to the gods of Mesopotamia, while all around you are Amun, Ptah and Hathor. The neighbours invite you to their festival and say that Ishtar and Hathor are really the same goddess under different names.
ev.ane_f_egyptian_abroad.convert: Bring offerings to the local gods
ev.ane_f_egyptian_abroad.title: Far from the Nile
ev.ane_f_egyptian_abroad.text: There are no temples of Amun here, and nobody knows how to bury the dead properly. The neighbours advise you to seek the protection of the local gods: "Marduk is kind even to foreigners."
ev.ane_f_maat.amend: Make peace with those you wronged
ev.ane_f_maat.title: The weighing of the heart
ev.ane_f_maat.text: More and more often you dream of the judgement of Osiris: your heart on the scales against the feather of Maat. "I have not taken bread from the hungry, I have not lied…" you repeat, and you are not sure of all of it.
ev.ane_f_ishtar_statue.scoff: Scoff: we have our own gods
ev.ane_f_ishtar_statue.title: Ishtar of Nineveh
ev.ane_f_ishtar_statue.text: They say the king of Mitanni has sent the ailing Pharaoh the statue of Ishtar of Nineveh to heal him. The statue is carried through the city, and people bring their sick children to the roadside.
